title: Claude's PowerShell tool calls are invisible to Engram check evidence and overlap tracking
outcome:
Reported by Engram::Opus (session-7284, mailbox #190, 2026-09-25). After the restart, Engram opened a test obligation for source edits in root session-7284 and kept it open. The session had run `cargo test --lib` twice through the Claude PowerShell tool (1016 and 1019 passed) and run two launcher full gates.

Cause, from the code: the Claude adapter records a command only for the "Bash" tool (src/claude.rs:1780 start, :1848 result). The PowerShell tool reaches neither recorder.command_started_in nor the command-completion path. So on Windows, where Claude sessions often use PowerShell:
(1) a test run through PowerShell never becomes typed Test verification evidence (tm-winf step 2), and the Engram source_mutation_requires_test obligation cannot be met that way;
(2) a PowerShell command that writes into a worktree does not count as a running command, so it does not mark an overlapping check in that worktree as unknown. That is an evidence-soundness gap, not only a missing feature.

Fix direction: treat the PowerShell tool like Bash in the Claude adapter: command_started_in with the command line, and completion with an exit mapped like engram_claude_command_exit. The PowerShell result format has to be confirmed first, since it may not use Bash's "Exit code N" prefix. Recognition already handles a pwsh-wrapped command. Directory tracking would need a pwsh reading (Set-Location/cd/Push-Location), or else declining to credit when the cwd is unknown. Tests: a PowerShell cargo test recorded as passed; a PowerShell write during a check marks it overlapped.

Workaround until then: run tests through the Bash tool in the foreground and end the turn.
